name: Korquel
description: Long-range scopes flagged Korquel for its K-class signature, brighter than its mass allows. Resonant chains lock the middle planets into a slow stately dance visible over decades. Something in the belt reflects too regularly, and the guild pays for a second look.

stars.name: Bright Cinder
stars.description: A K-class star burning orange, the dependable engine of its court. Surface granulation churns visibly, and flare seasons come like clockwork. Its wind shapes every orbit in the system, and the weather follows it.

planets.name: Tidefell
planets.description: Lava lakes breathe through a fractured crust, resurfacing yearly. Sulfur frost rims the high ground between the glowing rifts. A standing bounty covers any intact core sample from the second planet outward.

moons.name: Obsidian Basalt I
moons.description: A battered companion keeping patient orbit through the ages. Tidal stress warms its interior, and frost cracks map the strain. Outgassing vents frost the trailing face a little more each orbit.

planets.name: Silentshallows
planets.description: Cracked highlands sprawl beneath a thin sky, every crater a kept record. Dust devils wander the basins, and the night side glitters with ice. A standing bounty covers any intact core sample from the second planet outward.

moons.name: Quartz Pumice I
moons.description: A battered companion keeping patient orbit through the ages. Tidal stress warms its interior, and frost cracks map the strain. Shepherd resonances with the rings betray a denser core than expected.

moons.name: Silent Pumice III
moons.description: A battered companion keeping patient orbit through the ages. Its surface records every era of bombardment the system ever knew. Outgassing vents frost the trailing face a little more each orbit.

planets.name: Quartzdeep
planets.description: Temperate bands of green and gold suggest a biosphere in full swing. Settlement charters queue for landing windows every season. Something in the belt reflects too regularly, and the guild pays for a second look.

planets.name: The Meridian hollow
planets.description: Banded clouds race around a deep crushing interior of metallic hydrogen. Its ring shepherds keep the lanes clear and the rumors plentiful. The guild maintains a listening post here, though no report has ever named its purpose.

planets.name: Broadfell
planets.description: Cracked highlands sprawl beneath a thin sky, every crater a kept record. Mining cuts stripe the equator where the crust proved thinnest. One moon occults on a schedule that matches no ephemeris, and navigators plan around it.

moons.name: Vapor Pebble I

planets.name: Tidemark
planets.description: Banded clouds race around a deep crushing interior of metallic hydrogen. Storm ovals larger than worlds spin for centuries without fading. Salvage crews swear the comets arrive in formation, and the math almost agrees.

moons.name: Broad Flint II
moons.description: A battered companion keeping patient orbit through the ages. Tidal stress warms its interior, and frost cracks map the strain. Shepherd resonances with the rings betray a denser core than expected.

planets.name: Umbervast
planets.description: Methane haze wraps a slushy mantle, cold and blue and utterly calm. Diamond rain is theorized below, though no probe has returned to confirm. One moon occults on a schedule that matches no ephemeris, and navigators plan around it.

dwarfPlanets.name: Gilded Nether 55
dwarfPlanets.description: A small cold world holding its round shape against the dark. Frost plains stretch unbroken to a horizon that curves too soon. Its thin story is written entirely in impact craters.

asteroids.name: Pumice 821
asteroids.description: A tumbling rock with a scarred face and a patient spin. Its regolith hides metal concentrations the assays prize. Outgassing cracks suggest ice beneath the dust mantle.

comets.name: Wandering Mourner
comets.description: A dirty snowball falling sunward on its long appointed round. Each passage sheds glittering debris the scopes track for seasons. Its tail leans away from the star like a banner in a gale.
